Could be a tally. - Secret family? ### Languages - Common - Vedalken - Thieves' Cant ### Physical Attributes - Harengon - 35 years old - Height: 4'1" - Weight: 185 lb. ### Important Connections - **[Mirian Faremeadow](#/page/mirian-faremeadow)** (Mom | Harengon) - **[Hargrim Krakensbain](#/page/hargrim-krakensbain)**, (Captain and Father Figure | Dwarf, Male) - Old Missive pigeon - Gifted to him by his mother - The gift was meant to give him a being to care for, to help him not be so afraid - **[Quinton Morgan](#/page/quinton-morgan)**, (Former First Mate | ???, Male) - **[The Black Fleet](#/page/the-black-fleet)** - They think he's dead, but they never forgive. If they see him, they will finish the job. ### Summary - Actual name is **Barduk Faremeadow** - Father died in a pirate raid when he was young - Lived alone with **[Mirian Faremeadow](#/page/mirian-faremeadow)**, his mother, in a small coastal fishing village. Wonders if **she's still alive?** - Taken in a random pirate raid when he was a child - Held onto the **broken missive pigeon** **[Mirian](#/page/mirian-faremeadow)** gave him as a child - **[The Black Fleet](#/page/the-black-fleet)** raided those pirates, and **[Hargrim Krakensbain](#/page/hargrim-krakensbain)** took him in as a cabin boy - **[Hargrim Krakensbain](#/page/hargrim-krakensbain)** became a father figure to him, and nicknamed him **Scrimshank** because he moved so slowly with fear - **[Hargrim Krakensbain](#/page/hargrim-krakensbain)** taught him to fight, and how to lead - Took the name **Skrimhawk** as a nod to his father figure’s nickname for him and his [mother](#/page/mirian-faremeadow)'s gift, the **broken missive pigeon** - Received a note from **[Hargrim Krakensbain](#/page/hargrim-krakensbain)** saying "*The freedom I fought for is finally mine*" stamped with his insignia of a **kraken pierced by two crossing harpoons** - Decided to risk death and abandon **[The Black Fleet](#/page/the-black-fleet)** - Shared this with his **first mate** **[Quinton Morgan](#/page/quinton-morgan)**, who betrayed him and forced him to **walk the plank** - After several weeks adrift at sea, he was picked up by an **[East Claw Trading Company](#/page/east-claw-trading-company)** ship which brought him to a **[The Broken Wing](#/page/the-broken-wing) House** in **[Hocku Port](#/page/hocku-port)** ### Submitted Backstory Skrimhawk was a paladin devoted to [The Black Fleet](#/page/the-black-fleet) pirates and he is breaking his oath to them and leaving. Being a pirate is all he has ever known since he was a cabin boy for an old legendary pirate and rose through the ranks carving out his own place in the fleet. Having plundered and looted to his hearts content, he asked himself if this was all there is to life. Nothing would bring him joy and life at sea had become monotonous. Leaving the organization, however, is punishable by death. He was betrayed by his first mate who he had entrusted his plans to and was promptly caught. His sentence was to walk the plank. He was adrift at sea for several weeks holding on to a piece of driftwood and using fish as sustenance. He was picked up by a ship from the [East Claw Trading Company](#/page/east-claw-trading-company) who brought him to [Hocku Port](#/page/hocku-port). Questions Organization: The Black Fleet (A group of the most feared pirates in all the land and sea) Legendary captain: [Hargrim Krakensbain](#/page/hargrim-krakensbain) (old retired Dwarven pirate captain) basically Skrimhawk's "Mr. Miyagi" Skrimhawk thought he was dead, but received a note saying "The freedom I fought for is finally mine" stamped with an insignia of a kraken pierced by two crossing harpoons. This note is what set him on his current path. Skrimhawk seeks freedom above all else. He wants to find out how Hargrim escaped the pirate life if this note was truly from his old captain. First mate: [Quinton Morgan](#/page/quinton-morgan). Once a trusted ally, he betrayed Skrimhawk to the Black Fleet when he learned of his plans to leave. **What is he looking for now? Redemption? Love? Something Different?** He seeks freedom above all else. He hopes to find his old captain to this end. His whole life has been spent under the rule of others. Despite making a name for himself as a pirate captain, he still was under the black fleets rule. He seeks to become the master of his own fate. **Who does he know outside of the pirates?** [Hargrim Krakensbain](#/page/hargrim-krakensbain). He had a mother before being taken but he knows nothing about where she could be or if she was alive. He hasn't seen or heard of her in 25 years **Optional quirk-building prompt: what does he enjoy that he doesn’t want people to know about?** He loves a good story from a stranger but he loves a bottle of rum far more. He doesn't drink often because when he does, he tends to overshare. **Does he plan on facing “the sins” in his past?** In his mind he was always a fair captain and to an extent he was right. [Hargrim](#/page/hargrim-krakensbain) was the closest thing to a good role model he has ever had. Until he develops and accurate moral compass he won't even see his actions as sins much less confront them. (I hope we have some kind of good aligned character to help him out with this). **Does he plan on facing the people in his past, or hiding from them?** [Hargrim](#/page/hargrim-krakensbain) is priority one but he has no idea where to start. [The Black Fleet](#/page/the-black-fleet)] will eventually catch up to him unless he finds a way to deter them. He will definitely have to face off against Quinton Morgan at some point and find out if any of his old crew would take his side. His mother could come into the picture later on at some point. ### Do - [ ] Work out details with David - [ ] Add Thieves' Cant and Dwarven to languages - [ ] More knives! Don't be afraid of the past sins! - [ ] What species was Quinton Morgan? Tiefling - [ ] Skrimhawk is the "military police" / enforcers of the black fleet - The Crimson Wake is the ship that does this - [ ] Grew up with Quinton and Roxie - [ ] Not two levels of pirates, black fleet was the only pirate crew he interacted with - [ ] Roxie: Harengon - Subdued and cool-headed - Wild card: he doesn't know if she betrayed him or if Quinton found his plans - Hates the pirate life - Navigator and quartermaster - Skrimhawk is getting older, the lies that he tells himself have begun to weigh on him. Without Hargrim's guidance, he strays more and more away from goodness - Received the letter from Hargrim. Brings back a sense of dead morals - He sees his father's murder reflected in his own hands - Plans an escape - [ ] The Mouth of Crimson - Serpent and man mirror each other

# Obsidian-First Game-Day Prep Architecture

> [!abstract]+ THE GOAL
> **Prep for random access, not for reading order.**  
> Your prose can stay rich. The change is that prose should sit *inside a scene unit* with a small control layer above it, while a separate game-day dashboard tells you what can happen next.

The current long-form arc notes are strong as writing documents, but on game day they ask your brain to do three jobs at once: remember where information is buried, decide what scene is relevant, and run the scene. Obsidian can take the first two jobs off your plate.

## The Smallest Change That Gives the Biggest Return

Do **not** rebuild the whole vault first.

Add only three things:

1. A folder or note group for **Scenes**.
2. One **Game Day — Current** dashboard.
3. One **Scene Template**.

Keep your existing NPC, location, faction, magic, and arc notes. Migrate a scene only when you are about to run it or substantially revise it.

---

# 1. Make Scenes the Unit You Run

A session is chronological. Your campaign is not.

A **scene note** should answer: *If the players choose this right now, can I run it without hunting through another document?*

A good scene note contains:

- the trigger that makes it relevant;
- the one-sentence purpose;
- the read-aloud / event prose you already write well;
- what the NPCs want **right now**;
- information that must land vs. information that is optional;
- mechanics that can interrupt RP;
- exits to other scenes;
- a fallback if the players bypass the expected entrance.

> [!tip]+ Important distinction
> **Locations are not scenes.** `[Nox Observatory](#/page/nox-observatory)` should hold stable facts about Nox Observatory. A note like `Scene - Celeste Returns to Nox` holds what is happening *this time the party goes there*.
>
> **NPCs are not scenes.** `[Maeve Efthalia](#/page/maeve-efthalia)` holds stable character information. `Scene - Maeve Asks Celeste for the Verdict` holds the immediate dramatic problem.

---

# 2. Give Every Scene Properties

Use Properties so Obsidian can sort and filter scenes without you maintaining a manual master list.

```yaml
---
type: scene
status: ready
arc: "[The Monster in the Lava - The Soul Eater](#/page/the-monster-in-the-lava-the-soul-eater)"
location:
  - "[The Silver City](#/page/the-silver-city)"
spotlight:
  - "[Spark - Voli Flintrest](#/page/spark-voli-flintrest)"
npcs:
  - "[The Gate Guardian](#/page/the-gate-guardian)"
scene_kind:
  - reveal
  - roleplay
priority: high
can_skip: true
---
```

### Suggested property vocabulary

**`status`**
- `seed` — idea only
- `prep` — needs work
- `ready` — can be run now
- `active` — currently unfolding / unresolved
- `resolved` — happened at the table
- `retired` — no longer relevant but did not happen

**`scene_kind`**
- `roleplay`
- `reveal`
- `combat`
- `exploration`
- `travel`
- `choice`
- `downtime`

**`priority`**
- `high` — likely / important
- `normal`
- `low` — bonus material

Use **links** in Properties for entities (`arc`, `location`, `spotlight`, `npcs`) and plain text for state fields (`status`, `priority`, `scene_kind`).

> [!info]+ Why this matters
> Once scenes have consistent Properties, Obsidian's core **Bases** feature can show them as filtered/sorted tables, lists, or cards without requiring Dataview.

---

# 3. Use This Scene Template

Put this in your Templates folder as something like `Template - Scene.md`.

```markdown
---
type: scene
status: prep
arc:
location:
spotlight:
npcs:
scene_kind:
priority: normal
can_skip: true
---

# {{title}}

> [!abstract]+ RUN IN 10 SECONDS
> **Trigger:**
> **Purpose:**
> **Immediate pressure:**
> **Exit / handoff:**

^run

> [!danger]- DM SECRET
> What is true behind the curtain.
> Keep hypotheses or unsettled ideas labeled as such.

> [!question]- OPEN MYSTERY — DO NOT SOLVE FOR THE PLAYERS
> What should remain a question after this scene?

## What Everyone Wants

- **NPC:**
- **NPC:**
- **Party pressure:**

## Must Land

- [ ] Essential information / consequence.
- [ ] Essential decision or image.

## Optional Texture

- Details that can be dropped if the scene is dragging.
- Extra lore if players lean in.

## Read Aloud / Event Text

Your full descriptive prose stays here. Do not turn this into bullet-point mush just because the control layer is concise.

## Roleplay Prompts

> [!tip] Roleplay
> What do you do?

## Mechanics

- **Trigger:**
- **Roll:**
- **DC:**
- **On success:**
- **On failure:**

^mechanics

## If They Break the Expected Entrance

> [!example]- FLEXIBILITY, NOT CANON
> Move essential information to another credible carrier. Do not force the exact staging if the staging was optional.

## Exits

- If they pursue **A** → Scene - ...
- If they pursue **B** → Scene - ...
- If they leave → Scene - ...

^exits

## After the Session

- [ ] Set `status: resolved` or `retired`.
- [ ] Record only what actually became canon.
- [ ] Add new links created by player choices.
```

The human-readable block IDs (`^run`, `^mechanics`, `^exits`) let a dashboard jump directly to the exact part of a long note you need.

---

# 4. Build One Game-Day Dashboard

The dashboard should contain almost no prose. It is your cockpit.

```markdown
# Game Day — Current

> [!abstract]+ TONIGHT IN ONE BREATH
> One paragraph. No lore dump. What is happening *now*?

## Start Here
- Opening scene

## Ready Scenes
- Scene name — one-line reason it may happen
- Scene name — one-line reason it may happen

## Active Pressures
- Timar's tremors / city stability
- Ralora's sentencing
- Guardian contact

## Spotlight Queue
- Celeste —
- Skrimhawk —
- Spark —
- HAL —
- Kiktal —
- Flicker —

## Quick Mechanics
- Time-walk checks
- Library pulse save

## Open Hooks
- [ ]

## End-of-Session Capture
- [ ] What became canon?
- [ ] What scene state changed?
- [ ] What did a player care about that I did not expect?
```

### Better: let a Base populate the Ready Scenes list

If you split scenes into files, embed a core Obsidian Base directly in the dashboard:

```base
filters:
  and:
    - 'type == "scene"'
    - 'status != "resolved"'
    - 'status != "retired"'
views:
  - type: table
    name: Ready / Active Scenes
    order:
      - file.name
      - status
      - priority
      - location
      - spotlight
      - scene_kind
```

You can then add a second view filtered to `status == "ready"`, or group/sort however your brain wants on game day.

---

# 5. Use Transclusion as “Single Source of Truth”

You are already doing this in places, but it can be pushed further.

If `[The Grand Library](#/page/the-grand-library)` owns the stable physical description, a scene should embed that description rather than copy it:

```markdown
## Arrival
[The Grand Library](#/page/the-grand-library#Physical%20Description)
```

If `[The Nameless](#/page/the-nameless)` owns Zenny's research, keep the canonical research there and embed the relevant section into the scene:

```markdown
[The Nameless](#/page/the-nameless#Zenny's%20Studies%20on%20the%20Nameless)
```

**Rule:** the note that represents the thing owns the stable truth; the scene note owns what happens *today*.

This prevents three slightly different versions of the same room, NPC motive, or lore fact from drifting apart.

---

# 6. Use Aliases Aggressively for Names, Not Tags

Your campaign has characters with multiple names. Put those names in `aliases` so links resolve naturally.

Example for Voli:

```yaml
---
aliases:
  - Spark
  - Voli
  - Voli Flintrest
---
```

Example for Guardian:

```yaml
---
aliases:
  - Guardian
  - Gate Guardian
  - The Gate Guardian
---
```

Use tags for **categories**, not identities:

Good:
- `#prep/scene`
- `#arc/active`
- `#lore/faction`

Less useful:
- `#Guardian`
- `#Celeste`
- `#SilverCity`

Those should be `links`, because links give you backlinks and relationship context.

---

# 7. Standardize Callouts by Job

Your notes already use callouts, but giving each type a fixed job reduces scanning time.

> [!abstract]+ `[!abstract]+` — RUN IN 10 SECONDS
> Always open. The minimum needed to run the scene.

> [!danger]- `[!danger]-` — DM SECRET
> Collapsed by default. Truth the players should not receive as exposition.

> [!question]- `[!question]-` — OPEN MYSTERY
> Collapsed. What the scene should leave unresolved.

> [!tip]+ `[!tip]+` — ROLEPLAY / PLAYER PROMPT
> Open when it contains the next thing you actually say or ask.

> [!todo]- `[!todo]-` — PREP GAP
> Collapsed during play. Work for future-you, not table-you.

> [!example]- `[!example]-` — FLEXIBILITY OPTION
> Non-canon alternatives for when players break your expected route.

The important part is not the visual style; it is that your eye learns what each box means without reading it first.

---

# 8. Bookmarks: Make a Permanent “DM Rail”

Use Obsidian's Bookmarks core plugin for the things you should be able to reach without navigating the vault.

Recommended bookmarks:

- `Game Day — Current`
- current arc note
- current scene
- `Roll Tracker`
- `Magic & Energy`
- a bookmarked search for unfinished prep
- a bookmarked search for `status: ready` scenes if you do not use a Base

Useful saved searches include:

```text
[type:scene] [status:ready]
```

and:

```text
task-todo:
```

The point is to make “where is that?” a one-click problem.

---

# 9. Workspaces: Save a Game-Day Layout

Create a **Game Day** workspace separate from your **Prep** workspace.

### Game Day workspace

**Center:** `Game Day — Current`  
**Right sidebar:** Outline for the current scene + Backlinks as a linked view  
**Left sidebar:** Bookmarks + Search  
**Second tab group:** current location / NPC note  
**Optional pop-out:** rules, encounter tracker, or music note

### Prep workspace

**Center:** arc / scene you are editing  
**Right:** Backlinks + Outgoing links / Properties  
**Left:** File explorer + Search

The value is not aesthetic. A workspace lets you recover your whole DM layout after you have clicked through twenty notes during play.

---

# 10. Make “Skipped” a Valid Scene State

A nonlinear campaign gets painful when prep assumes every prepared scene must happen.

Do not measure prep success by “used all the content.”

For each scene, decide:

- **Essential information?** It may move.
- **Essential consequence?** It may occur offscreen if appropriate.
- **Optional staging?** Let it die if players skip it.
- **Character moment?** Never force it merely because you wrote it.

This is particularly useful for the Silver City material. The Trial, Academy, Nox Observatory, family reunion, and library do not all need the same level of inevitability. The library currently carries the strongest forward hook, so if its staging is skipped, preserve the hook without railroading the ceremony.

---

# 11. How I Would Restructure These Two Specific Notes

## Keep as arc notes

- `[The Humbling of the Silver City](#/page/the-humbling-of-the-silver-city)` — overview, stakes, links to component scenes.
- `[The Monster in the Lava - The Soul Eater](#/page/the-monster-in-the-lava-the-soul-eater)` — Vulk arc overview, DM secrets, open prep tasks, links to scenes.

## Promote these into scene notes first

1. `Scene - The Picnic`
2. `Scene - City Falling`
3. `Scene - Time Slowing`
4. `Scene - In a Quiet Room`
5. `Scene - Celeste Returns Home`
6. `Scene - Ralora Trial`
7. `Scene - Library Room Dedication`
8. `Scene - Voli's Sending Echoes`
9. `Scene - Choosing the Route to Vulk`
10. `Scene - Vulk Steel Hull Entrance`

These are the places where you currently have either dense prose, a meaningful choice, mechanics, or a reveal. Those are the notes most likely to make you search frantically at the table.

## Keep these as entity/location notes

- `[The Silver City](#/page/the-silver-city)`
- `[The Grand Library](#/page/the-grand-library)`
- `[Nox Observatory](#/page/nox-observatory)`
- `[Vulk Ildstad](#/page/vulk-ildstad)`
- `[The Nameless](#/page/the-nameless)`
- `[The Gate Guardian](#/page/the-gate-guardian)`
- `Soul Engines`
- `[Voyager Rails](#/page/voyager-rails)`
- `[Subspace](#/page/subspace)`

## Keep this as a dashboard / arc-control note

- `Silver City → Vulk Ildstad — Game-Day Master`

The merged master I created alongside this document is deliberately a **bridge format**: immediately useful as one file, but already organized around scene anchors so you can split it later without redesigning the logic.

---

# 12. A Migration Rule That Prevents Prep From Becoming a Second Job

> [!success]+ MIGRATE ONLY WHEN TOUCHED
> Never spend a weekend “fixing the vault.”
>
> When you open an old scene to prep it for an upcoming game:
> 1. move it into the Scene Template;
> 2. add its Properties;
> 3. replace duplicated stable lore with embeds;
> 4. link its exits;
> 5. mark it `ready`.
>
> Over time, the playable part of the vault becomes structured without forcing you to reorganize years of material all at once.

---

# 13. What Not to Optimize Away

Do **not** replace your descriptive passages with terse bullets. The prose is part of how you run this campaign.

Do **not** force every NPC thought into a database field. Properties are for retrieval, not for replacing characterization.

Do **not** pre-decide every branch. “If they do anything else” is better handled by strong NPC wants, clear pressures, and linked exits than by a giant flowchart.

Do **not** turn every lore sentence into its own note. Create a note when something needs its own identity, backlinks, reusable truth, or game-day retrieval point.

The target is simple: **when the players jump sideways, you should need one click—not one memory—to follow them.**

# Silver City → Vulk Ildstad — Game-Day Master

> [!abstract]+ LIZARD-BRAIN SUMMARY
> 1. **The Silver City survives**, but only after Skrimhawk walks backward through the last moments of the fall and Timar finally acts.
> 2. **The city is alive but destabilized:** physical damage, failed Peacekeepers, political collapse, Timar holding the rings, and tremors that make his condition impossible to ignore.
> 3. **Silver City scenes are modular:** Celeste's family, Ralora's trial, the Academy, Nox Observatory, and the library can be entered according to what the party pursues.
> 4. **The library is the cleanest forward-plot pivot:** Guardian's pauldron reacts with Flicker's boots while Voli's old Sendings suddenly lock onto Guardian and a broken plea comes back: “Spark... Help... Me... Vulk... Is...”
> 5. **The Vulk arc asks why Guardian can suddenly be reached, what the Nameless are doing in the ruins, and what the so-called Soul Eater actually is.**

^control-panel

> [!danger]- DM SECRETS — DO NOT LEAK AS EXPLANATION
> - The **Soul Eater is [The Gate Guardian](#/page/the-gate-guardian)**, killed in the Fall and returned as a corrupted distortion.
> - The current prep says [The Nameless](#/page/the-nameless) integrated a corrupted shard of binding into Guardian's lifeless shell.
> - Guardian has been taking souls from ruin-scavengers.
> - The sending failures are tied to Guardian flickering between states in which the spell does and does not have a valid recipient.

# <mark class="story">The Story so Far</mark>

<mark class="music">♫    -     ▸     4.1.1 Time Stretched Thin Like a Web      ↻¹</mark>

Pelotharna, a sunken city built on the bones of another.  
Eternis, a kingdom that disappeared.
The Megadome, a cocoon that never cracked.

Your adventures have taken you all across the surface of the Dragon’s Garden, and that is to say nothing of your treks through other planes, and the pockets between them.

You’ve saved a city overrun by a new breed of monstrosities. You’ve come face to face with a broken overseer, trapped in a divine prison. And you have subdued the heart of a new evil, in the hopes that your efforts might bring stability to the Silver City. A kingdom-sized meteor, teetering on the edge of a cloud.

It hasn’t been easy. It hasn’t been simple. And it hasn’t been clean.

In the last several hours alone, you've had to fight your way through the twisted, cackling mind of a demigod. You have become bound to each other through horrors that ordinary folks have no concept of. But you do. Because *you* do not have the luxury of ignorance. You've been asked to shoulder divine threats, choose between imperfect solutions, and face down the limits of your own mortality.

You are the Misfortune’s Misfits. A quilt woven of hope, tragedy, and gritted teeth. Has fate appointed you its champion? Or its jester? Moment to moment, her motives elude you.

All you know is that now, right now in this moment, you are falling.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Battle After Battle      ↻¹</mark>

You fall, and Belbe’s taunts echo through your head: “Do you wonder, who will the son of madness become next? Perhaps the little friends will stow the son of madness away somewhere safe. Somewhere far away from all the other tiny sprouts in the garden? But how long do the little friends imagine they could keep the son hidden? See you soon, little friends.”

Were these the ravings of a lunatic or the prophecy of a god? You were given no time to contend with this question as hundreds of tar-black wings sprouted from Belbe's seraphim form - closing around her, hardening - cocooning into an obsidian egg, with feathery reliefs.

Then, a vision took you. Or perhaps it was a conscious experience… Your sanity has been too frayed to distinguish one from the other. A dragonborn man draped in court jester’s clothes. He clapped and jingled and laughed at a spinning toy top, knocking it off balance with a sickly “topsy turvy!”

Now, in the sanctum of the lambs, gravity no longer has meaning. The ground beneath you might as well be the ceiling, or the walls. You’re caught somewhere between falling and floating, the city hitching and screeching against the failing chains of Marduun’s artifact. Cries of terror from the festival above overwrite every quiet moment.

You’ve done your part. You’ve subdued Belbe. And Valenthe has done hers. The machine has transposed the egg.

Now, Timar must do his part, if the Silver City is to survive. You’ve begged. You’ve pleaded with him. You appealed to whatever reason his fractured mind still holds. But he’s barely moved, barely bothered to even look up. He is free of the crypt, but his eyes are dim, and he doesn't believe it.

This is where we continue our story, with the rings of the city, the slums below, and perhaps all of De Drakengardt, at the mercy of an overseer whose mind was broken centuries ago.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.1 Featherfall      ↻¹</mark>

However. Celeste. Your mind is elsewhere.

# <mark class="story">Comings and Goings</mark>
You are approached by a city official, some poor gnome who seems like he's in way over his head [Punar Tillam](#/page/punar-tillam). He addresses you, attempting to fulfill his civic duty and take some sort of action. In a shaky voice, he manages a meager:

> [!Quote] Punar Tillam
> What happened down here?

> [!Quote] Punar Tillam
> Follow me, please. There is a great shock in the streets, but I cannot lose you in the chaos.
 
 His voice is pleading, sincere. 

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  + ⇥      4.1.1 Trio for Willa      ↻¹</mark>

The next moments are a blur.

As you come to the surface, you see wreckage. Many buildings… lie in *ruin*, toppled over by the jolting halts when the wizards chains failed. The peacekeepers do not move as they should. They hardly move at all. Dust covers the streets and stabs at your lungs.

The aftermath is a cold and heartless calm. Stunned citizens quietly cry and bleed and sit in a haze and look to the horizon. And you notice how much closer that horizon now sits. The city has fallen far from its proud heights.

Bodies lie still among the rubble. Some are attended to with wrappings and medical salves. Many are unconscious and perhaps many more are dead.

You glance beyond the city’s edge, where Timar stands on a cloudy perch, wings outstretched. The light of the moon and the stars refract through him like glittering waters. They form a soft halo at the edges his silhouette. It’s a majestic sight, but unrest twitches through him in erratic waves. Shivers that stab him, through his body, through his face. And each time, a hint of a tremor agitates the ground beneath your feet. But, the city holds.

[Punar](#/page/punar-tillam) leads you to a room within the high court and tells you "wait here." But his words are half-command, half-plea, like he's unsure if he's overstepping his rank. He steps out of the room, and closes the door. There’s a constant shuffling of muffled footsteps in the hallway outside.

<hr class="short">

The hours bleed into each other. Council members and officials coming and going, all in a frantic rush, often asking you the same things as those that had questioned you before them.

Questions like “Who are you,” and “what were you doing below,” and “how did you infiltrate the city” and “aren’t you the exiled daughter of Professor Efthalia,” and “weren’t you banished on account of the red professor’s death?” These questions all spew out at you, soaked in suspicion, but no one really knows what to do with your answers. They just nod, jot down a note, and leave you alone again.

# <mark class="story">Accomodations</mark>

The old wizard leads you out the door, where a man—some mix of gnomish and elven—stands guard. For Celeste and Hal, it’s a sight you’ve never seen before--a man standing guard. People don’t stand guard. That’s what Peacekeepers are for. But as you walk down the grandiose corridors of the high court, you realize there are no peacekeepers anywhere, and there should be. Here of all places, there always are.

A staircase at the end of a hall leads several stories up, and you exit into another hall. Narrower. Lined with the kind of long, thin windows that start at the floor and end in a pointed arch far above eye level. Rays of moonlight filter in, lazy and blurred like plucked strings on a harp.

The city rings outside lie still. Some of you catch a glimpse of a clock in the hall. Dawn is only an hour away, at most.

Down the hall, a man is placed outside one of the rooms, standing guard. Marduun stops at his door. There's a plaque on it that reads “Solveris”.

Marduun opens the door with a creak, ignoring the man.

There are eight beds inside, stacked atop each other in pairs of two.

Celeste, HAL, it strikes you as a room that might have been built as lodging for the family of a visiting dignitary, back in ancient times when the city still did that sort of thing. Generations before your lifetime.

It's all immaculately maintained despite its disuse. There’s a desk, probably carved from some great ancient wood pillaged from some great ancient forest in the north. A few lounging chairs and a fainting couch encircle a coffee table, all tastefully scattered about.

> [!quote] Marduun
Rest. I shall make your case personally in… whatever remains of the city's court system. Although… it may take some time. An exiled infiltrator and her cohorts may not be the subject that requires the most immediate attention, given the state of affairs.
>
Sleep. I will find you when the time is right.

With that, he steps into the hall, and closes the door.

> [!abstract]- GAME-DAY — Nothing Left but Our Words
> **Payoff:** formal release, apology, [Spellbook Jailbreak](#/page/spellbook-jailbreak), and Celeste seeing her parents. This scene can open directly into reunion RP.

^scene-nothing-left

# <mark class="story">Nothing Left but Our Words</mark>
<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.3 | Vovo e Vovo ↻¹</mark>

The days that followed felt as if they both dragged on *and* flew by, in the way that it can feel when you're trapped in a room and then passed around for questioning and then stuffed back into a room for safe keeping.

Eventually your testimony was requested in the high court. No trial was held against you. The evidence in your favor had mounted so completely that no trial was deemed necessary.

> [!quote] Veldrin Illiir 
"You are free to go."

Councilwoman of Innovation [Veldrin Illiir](#/page/councilwoman-veldrin-illiir) makes eye contact with each of you as she speaks. Cases like this are usually led by Councilman of Order [Soaruun Hun’ath](#/page/soaruun-hunath), but even from your sequestered quarters, you've heard rumors of his backroom deals with House [Ralora](#/page/castiel-ralora).

[Veldrin](#/page/councilwoman-veldrin-illiir) continues.

> [!quote] Veldrin Illiir 
But I do hope you’ll stay and allow us to repay you, if such a debt can be repaid. Especially you, Ms. Efthalia. There are no words of regret sincere enough to make whole the injustice lodged against you. And yet it seems we have little left *but* our words. However, Celeste, I would like to offer you a small token of my personal gratitude.

She holds a modified spellbook cartridge in her hand. An attendant takes it and walks it over to you:

>[Spellbook Jailbreak](#/page/spellbook-jailbreak)

> [!quote] Veldrin Illiir
I have been tinkering with for some time. Perhaps one day, once the Silver City has found its wings again, we may be able to offer you more. Thank you all.

Celeste, I'm not sure how much of Veldrin's words you would've heard. Because... Since you entered this room, your attention has been strained, due to the presence of two faces you haven’t seen since your exile... Your parents, Exander and Maeve Efthalia. They came to the hearing. You are all dismissed by the councilwoman and are free to go.

> [!tip] Roleplay
Celeste, what do you do?

Exander runs in and throws his arms around you, and he sobs. Maeve approaches you as unguarded and un-postured as you've ever seen from her, though it doesn't quite match your father's complete abandonment of his dignity.

> [!quote] Maeve
Celeste, I don’t have the words to… I.. I am... It is good to see you.

Exander can't seem to do anything but sob as he holds you.

> [!tip] Roleplay

> [!quote] Exander
HAL, I thought you were lost!

> [!abstract]- GAME-DAY — Home Bittersweet Home
> **Family RP sandbox:** the house itself shows the damage without being destroyed. Available threads: Exander notices HAL is different; parents meet the newer travelers; the party can finally explain where they have been.

# <mark class="story">Home Bittersweet Home</mark>

> [!success] Marduun
> Come. This is no place for a reunion.

or

> [!failure] Marduun
> Come. This is no place for such things.

You follow the old wizard through the streets, the sunlight offering what warmth it can to the battered city. Timar is still aloft beyond the city's edge, a quiet anchor for the three rings. His eyes are fixed somewhere beyond the horizon. A shudder runs through him, as a tremor pulses through the ground beneath your feet.

Celeste, Hal. You arrive. Home.

It's a manor tucked between manors, like books on a shelf. The stone threshold above the door is cracked. The crack runs up along the entire exterior. Not deep, not structural, but a visible scar from the city’s brush with collapse.

> [!tip] Roleplay
> What do you do?

Inside, things are mostly the way you remember them to be. Except the frames that *were* on the wall are all destroyed and the intricate plates and serving ware, are all shattered. Almost nothing delicate survived.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     2. Mood Nostalgic | pokopoko</mark>

> [!tip] Roleplay
> But you're home. What now?

> [!example] Maeve and Exander to the Party:
> - Exander notices HAL seems different (explore his new soul)
> - Who are these new travelers?
> - What have you been doing?

>

^scene-trial

# <mark class="story">📌 The Trial</mark>
<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.3 | Thaw ↻¹</mark>

Days in the Silver City turn into weeks. There have been almost no efforts to rebuild, only to clear the rubble, and recover the bodies within.

An ad hoc council is formed, composed of select Silver City citizens and leaders across the lands below, including the Buoy, and The Megadome’s president Olander Sunpearl. It’s strange to see foreign leaders enter the city, and many citizens seem uneasy with the amount of outsiders now being granted entrance.

[Maeve](#/page/maeve-efthalia), Celeste’s mother, is asked to sit at this new table. [Councilwoman Veldrin Illiir](#/page/councilwoman-veldrin-illiir), who took your testimony, leads the discussions on how to proceed as a city. Timar holds the city aloft, but the debate centers around whether this is a sustainable solution, given the tremors, and whether it might be best to lower the rings fully, and integrate with the lands below.

However, the topic requiring the most immediate attention is [Castiel Ralora](#/page/castiel-ralora), the man at the center of the injustices. He is tried in the high court, alongside several other highborns who played a role in keeping the truth hidden. Their trials are attended by citizens, outsiders, and many who lost family or friends to the Sanctum of the Lambs. Would you attend Ralora’s trial?

Ralora stands proud in the center of the room. Though he does avoid the gaze of the onlookers--the ones victimized by his actions. Still, there hasn’t been a single hint of remorse in him.

> [!quote] Castiel Ralora
> For generations, House Ralora has kept us afloat. It has been our solemn vow to the three rings. “Though the cost may be great, the cause is greater.” This has been our creed. It is a burden, yes, and it is one we have spared the city. You believe *that* pretender of godhood floating outside is the answer? He barely remembers his own name! No! It is my house that gave us our wings.
> 
> The three rings were built on the blood-sacrifice of those below\! We rose from the surface on their shoulders\! We were kept safe from the mad god\!
> 
> And what? Now, because you see a little blood on the scythe, you want to condemn the harvester? Your hands are only clean because of the blood under my fingernails. Under my father's fingernails. And his father before him.
> 
> WE KEPT YOUR HANDS CLEAN.
> 
> WE KEPT YOU OUT OF THE DIRT.

Ralora is heard. They convene for the day, and a few men cuff Castiel Ralora and begin to lead him back to his cell.

> [!tip] Roleplay
What do you do?

> [!example] • • •
> - Maeve asks Celeste's opinion on a verdict for Ralora
> - Guilty of what, exactly, is debated. No Silver City law covers the scope of House Ralora’s generational atrocities.
> - Maeve is the swing vote on Ralora’s sentencing, and asks for Celeste’s opinion.

# <mark class="story">The Library Room Dedication</mark>
- Punar approaches, letting the heroes know a room of the library has been dedicated to them, and a there will be a small surprise ceremony.

You travel the concentric streets of Luna, past several beautifully adorned municipal buildings, and [The Grand Library](#/page/the-grand-library) comes into view.

> [Read physical description](#/page/the-grand-library)

A red ceremonial ribbon is tied between two cracked pillars.

A small crowd is gathered. The lore-keeper, the city's equivalent to the head librarian, is among them: [Umtor Presven](#/page/umtor-presven). Celeste, he meets your eyes with a warm smile and steps up to a small podium.

> [!quote] Umtor Presven
I would like to call the "Misfortunes Misfits" to the podium next to me, if you would?
>
Fellow Silvians, it is my great honor to dedicate our primary study room to these heroes! Misfortune's Misfits, we are in your eternal debt. This gesture is but a fraction of what you deserve, but I do hope it can serve as a sign of our gratitude.
>
We've also asked those that are able, to add what coin they can spare to a pool. Once again, it cannot begin to truly repay you for your bravery, your sacrifice.

Celeste, he hands you a small decorative box. Silver, engraved with constellations you'd recognize. Inside, you find 300 platinum coins.

> [!quote] Umtor Presven
Now, I would not presume to take any more of your time in the name of pageantry!

He picks up a pair of large silver shears.

> [!quote] Umtor Presven
I hereby dedicate the primary reading room of our Grand Library to the six heroes of "Misfortunes Misfits!"

A cheer moves across the small crowd, and Umtor cuts through the red ribbon.

> [!quote] Umtor Presven
Shall I show you to your study room, heroes?

Once inside, the next few moments happen very quickly.

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     4.1.3 | Intrepid ↻¹</mark>

Spark, among the relics on display, one catches your eye, because it does not belong here in this floating city. It's a broken piece of a shoulder pauldron. It's [Vulkian](#/page/vulk-ildstad). The plaque makes no mention of [Vulk Ildstad](#/page/vulk-ildstad), but you'd recognize the design anywhere. And a closer look confirms it: this piece of armor belonged to your friend, [The Gate Guardian](#/page/the-gate-guardian). A thousand thoughts fire off all at once, trying to wrap an explanation around what you're seeing, why it's here, what it means.

In this same moment, Flicker, your [boots](#/page/gearlock-stompers) flash with a booming pulse. Two pulses. The third pulse is so intense it sends a shockwave outward, passing through your body, and rumbling the nearby shelves, and every one of you along the way. Your "father's" words repeat themselves in your mind, a harsh mental loop: steal divinity, share immortality, steal divinity, share immortality, steal divinity, share immortality.

Spark, you barely register the building chaos around you, because your attention is pulled inward to the part of you that casts magic and senses it's flow... Specifically, to each sending spell you've sent into the ether, for your old friend [Guardian](#/page/the-gate-guardian); each time you felt it spiral and sputter away into gods know where; each one you thought fell silently into abyss; they all snap into formation all at once like strings pulled taught. New threads that run *stable* from every word of every cast, directly to [Guardian](#/page/the-gate-guardian)'s ears.

Flicker: the pulses are strengthening. There's a fourth pulse, a fifth, and it's becoming unbearable the way it rattles your ribcage. Your boots twitch in sync with the pauldron-relic in the glass casing. It answers each pulse, vibrating and blurring; just as unstable as your boots. You've learned through past experience when artifacts cause this kind of reaction: either you put distance between yourself and that relic right now, or the pulses will build into something truly destructive.

>[!tip] Roleplay
>Flicker, what are you doing, right now?

<hr class="long">

**Constitution Saving Throw** <sup>DC 12</sup>
{.mechanics}

I need everyone to make a **Constitution Saving Throw** as pulse number 6 cracks the glass casing on each pedestals, and rips through your core.
{.mechanics}

Flicker, you'll make this throw at **disadvantage**, because you're wearing the source of the disruptions. Spark, you'll also be rolling at **disadvantage** because in this moment, your attention is split.
{.mechanics}

> [!failure]
> You take 15 points of force damage.

<hr class="long">

Spark, a response comes, and it's Guardian's voice, but the voice comes as frail as an injured animal:

> [!quote] Guardian
Spark... Help... Me... Vulk... Is...

The message recoils and collapses in on itself, unfinished.

>[!tip] Roleplay
>Spark, you've just heard [Guardian](#/page/the-gate-guardian)'s voice for the first time since the ancient era, what do you do?

# <mark class="story">Voli's Sending</mark>
[Voli](#/page/spark-voli-flintrest), since you've entered [The Silver City](#/page/the-silver-city), something curious has been happening. Weeks ago, you sent a message, through the weave, to Guardian. At the time, it spiraled into nothing. But the moment you stepped onto [The Silver City](#/page/the-silver-city), you heard your own words fly past you like debris in a tornado.

> [!quote]+ Voli
>Hello Guardian. Are you still there? What has happened? This is Voli. I’m so scared and alone.

It has happened several times since then. Your own words looping back through your mind.

> [!quote]+ Voli
>Hello Guardian. Are you still there? What has happened? This is Voli. I’m so scared and alone.

Easy enough to write off as [Belbe](#/page/belbe-the-son-of-madness)'s mind games.

> [!quote]+ Voli
>Hello Guardian. Are you still there? What has happened? This is Voli. I’m so scared and alone.

But here's the thing. It hasn't stopped. Belbe is sealed away in his father's crypt to the north. And yet, your words come back to you, once or twice a day.

> [!quote]+ Voli
>Hello Guardian. Are you still there? What has happened? This is Voli. I’m so scared and alone.

So why do you keep hearing them? It's not Belbe, that much you've determined through your experience of the arcane. But that's as far as you've gotten.

## Zenny's Studies on the Nameless
<hr class="short">
<hr class="short">

### A few scribbled notes, written in Zenny's handwriting:
"I know where rests a vast rotten thing. Its marrow is a feral magic ripe for harvest. It's bone a putrid stench of might. My Wyrm, my beloved Wyrm has provided us a blade to sharpen."
^ Was this written by **The Allmother?**

<center>~</center>

Are The Nameless refugees or invaders? I think I found evidence of a sisterhood fleeing their home in some astral reef, as an ancient Pale Wyrm swallowed it for a thousand years. Moment to moment, it's hard to tell.

<center>~</center>

**"The Great Work"**

### Written by [Fid Sundew](#/page/fid-sundew), the Scholar:
A carved graft of the Pale Wyrm whispered to the Allmother as she steered the Great Needle, silently puncturing into new realities unnoticed. Her people were a mosquito in the night. Quiet, numbing, gorging themselves on each scent of new air. The needle dulled, marooning them here in the weeds of the Dragon's Garden.

<center>~</center>

They live among us now. Have they have abandoned their calling? Perhaps. But hear me: *this does not matter*, for they have not abandoned their cunning. I feel l the knife that rests at our throat, and I dare not scream too loudly.

<hr class="short">

> Small minds might call what we do evil. Throw away this word, dear sister. We have no need of it. The dichotomy of good and evil serves only those too craven to act.
> 
> Remember this: the needle that pierces fabric thinks not of morality. You are a seamstress, and before you lies a fabric of possibility. *Sew*."

<center>~</center>

> An egg, dearest sister!
> 
> This is a real solution, one we can prune and shape. Our last attempt wasn't ripe, it was rotten. Our late Allmother gave her ear to her wyrm, all the while it tied a blindfold over her reason. I will make no such mistake. My eyes are open.

> The black egg is an unwritten prophecy, and this time I will be certain we are the ones holding the quill.
> 
> I have planted it in the sky. With a little water and a little patience, I believe it will bloom. Then we will pluck it and finally shake the dust of these lands from our boots.

# Physical Description
The campus is has such a large footprint that can be seen from almost anywhere in the three rings.

<hr class="long">

### Campus Exterior
You're met by a large marble courtyard with an impressive fountain at it's center. The sculpture that used to adorn it lies crumbled to the side, likely destroyed in the city's recent slip.

The Primary Hall sits regal and stoic behind the fountain, atop it's throne of stairs. Dozens of class buildings and learning centers and arcanist laboratories and collegiate libraries all sprawl outward between the manicured landscapes and walkways.


### Applied Spellcraft & Design
#### Exterior
As one of the first Departments added to the academy, the classrooms and labs of Applied Spellcraft & Design are not far from the school's center. This cluster of buildings always used to require more maintenance due to their age, and it looks like the slip has not been easy on them. One classroom has collapsed, leaving only half a wall still standing.

The lab you frequented, the one with [Professor Marduun](#/page/professor-allao-marduun)'s old office looks different from the last time you saw it. You remember the blackened stone, seared and marred from the fire used to frame you for the [professor](#/page/professor-allao-marduun)'s death.

The soot and discoloration is gone, but two separate cracks split it's sides open. They're wide enough to walk through.

<hr class="short">

#### Interior
Spellbooks and equipment lie toppled and broken. Little piles of rubble sit beneath fresh holes in the ceiling. The stench of speckle bites your nose. It's leaking from the various artificery. Air, which feels a bit unstable, as if half-written spells might also be leaking out.

Rolling hills, massive farming machines of old.
The volcano where [Vulk Ildstad](#/page/vulk-ildstad) was built, and where it's ruins now lie.

#### Exterior
As you head to the Capital Ring's center, the density of clustered buildings gives way to lush green lawns, carefully planted and meticulously manicured. Exotic flora, imported from the lands below, is tastefully scattered here and there, under the tall, sturdy trees. 

It's all arranged to frame the crown jewel of [The Silver City](#/page/the-silver-city): Nox Observatory. A towering symbol of the city's ambition, a monolith of its pride. You can see it's beautiful golden dome even from the surface below, it's golden dome like a second sun. It's breathtaking.

The cylindrical exterior is etched with the celestial bodies of the night sky. Constellations that move in unison with their counterparts above. It's tuned to perfect accuracy.

A calm breeze dances through.

#### Interior
The interior is a Valhalla of beauty. Majestic murals bring to life allegorical accounts of the three rings, the , The Silver City. They are inscrutable; even when they were explained to you, Celeste, they never formed into anything with real substance. But they are elegantly crafted. A pearlescent staircase spirals upward along the outer curved wall, supported by nothing, yet perfectly stable.

A central pillar of golden gears click and chunk quietly, keeping the city calendar accurate and true. Without them, the etched exterior would fall out of sync with the stars above. A few of your fellow students have *tried* to catch any *minute* imprecision, attempting to win the considerably large error bounty. But no one ever has, as far as you know.

Up in the dome, the whirring and ticking from below hushes, replaced by a soft, droning melody like a whale's call. The stars above, filtered into sound that mortals can hear. Useful data for arcanists of the sky; a cosmic lullaby for everyone else.

An immense Celestial telescope sits in the center, a dense mass of gold gears and glass lenses and Speckle veins. A lense twice the size of your body slots in as another slots out of place. There's no one at it's control panel, but it still ticks, observes, records. At its heart is a crown of glass, spinning, moving against the gears that sprawl outward and power the mammoth machine.
A seedy place outside the walls of [The Sunken City](#/page/the-sunken-city-pelotharna).

Like staring directly into what's normally blurred at the corners of your vision, stretched across a boiling horizon. Subspace seems like it was never meant to be traversed by things that can die.

# Physical Description
#### Exterior
It's exterior is a towering thing, with pillars four stories high framing it's impressive arched doors. Carvings border the roofline, depict [The Silver City](#/page/the-silver-city)'s retelling of world-history.

#### Interior
Inside, the first thing that hits you is the smell of ancient pages, parchments, and leather bindings. The next thing is the floor to ceiling shelves of books, with sliding ladders that patrons are discouraged from using. The space is vast, and still completely filled with books.

The foyer is lit by a regal chandelier the size of two owlbears.

Just inside are several several pedestal displays of thick glass, each showcasing various relics and items of curio. All of them contain magic that has long gone dormant.

<hr class=short>

###### 1. Small Prince's Crown
A crude iron crown sized for a child, too heavy for a mortal to wear comfortably. The inner rim is padded with faded red cloth, stained where little hands must have gripped it.

###### 2. Face with no Features
A marble portrait of a serene elven face, split in half. Hollowed out in the center Its face is polished smooth from centuries of touching. This was perhaps built to contain a precious arcane relic, as latent magic still leaks from the inside.

###### 3. War Banner
A ceremonial war banner preserved in a glass column of saltwater. The cloth has lost all color except one burgundy thread, which traces the shape of a closed fist with beams of light streaking out from the center. The symbol of [Crimson the Depraved](#/page/crimson-the-depraved), and a solemn reminder of the savagery below.

###### 4. Null Clock
A porcelain white clock device with thirteen hands and no numbers. Each hand is permanently fixed at the same hour: which we believe translates to something like "Null."

###### 5. Broken Pauldron of a Large Construct
Reflective obsidian black metals contrasts the snowy white paint, from the Ancient Era. We are unable to explain how the paint has not faded.

###### The Other Displays
The rest of the pedestals are empty. The didn't used to be.

# 1: Entrance And Guardian
There needs to be a reason why your dungeon hasn’t been plundered before or why the PCs are the heroes for the job. A guardian or challenge at the entrance is a good justification why the location remains intact. Also, a guardian sets up early action to capture player interest and energize a session.

**Room One challenge ideas:**

- The entrance is trapped.
- The entrance is cleverly hidden.
- The entrance requires a special key, such as a ceremony, command word, or physical object.
- The guardian was deliberately placed to keep intruders out. Examples: a golem, robot, or electric fence.
- The guardian is not indigenous to the dungeon and is a tough creature or force who’s made its lair in room one.
- The entrance is hazardous and requires special skills and equipment to bypass. For example: radiation leaks, security clearance, wall of fire.

Room One is your opportunity to establish mood and theme to your dungeon, so dress it up with care.

# 2: Puzzle Or Roleplaying Challenge

The PCs are victorious over the challenge of the first room and are now presented with a trial that cannot be solved with steel. This keeps problem solvers in your group happy and breaks the action up for good pacing.

Make Room Two a puzzle, skill-based, or roleplaying encounter, if possible. Room Two should shine the limelight on different PCs than Room One, change gameplay up, and offer variety between the challenge at the entrance and the challenge at the end.

> Note: if Room One was this type of encounter, then feel free to make Room Two combat-oriented. Room Two should allow for multiple solutions to prevent the game from stalling.

**Room Two ideas:**

- Magic puzzle, such as a chessboard tile floor with special squares.
- An AI blocks access to the rest of the complex and must be befriended, not fought.
- A buzzer panel for all the apartments, but the person the PCs are looking for has listed themselves under a different name, which can be figured out through previous clues you’ve dropped.
- A concierge at the front desk must be bluffed or coerced without him raising the alarm.
- A dirt floor crawls with poisonous snakes that will slither out of the way to avoid open flame. (A few might follow at a distance and strike later.)
- The PCs must convince a bouncer to let them in without confiscating their weapons.

Once you’ve figured out what Room Two is, try to plant one or more clues in Room One about potential solutions.

This ties the adventure together a little tighter, will delight the problem solvers, and can be a back-up for you if the players get stuck.

# 3: Trick or Setback
The purpose of this room is to build tension. Do this using a trick, trap, or setback. For example, after defeating a tough monster, and players think they’ve finally found the treasure and achieved their goal, they learn they’ve been tricked and the room is a false crypt.

Depending on your game system, use this room to cater to any player or character types not yet served by the first two areas. Alternatively, give your group a double-dose of gameplay that they enjoy the most, such as more combat or roleplaying.

**Room Three ideas:**

- The PCs rescue several prisoners or hostages. However, the victims might be enemies in disguise, are booby-trapped, or create a dilemma as they plead to be escorted back to safety immediately.
- A collapsed structure blocks part of the area. The debris is dangerous and blocks nothing of importance, another trap, or a new threat.
- Contains a one-way exit (the PCs must return and deal with Rooms One and Two again). i.e. Teleport trap, one-way door, 2000 foot water slide trap.
- The PCs finally find the artifact required to defeat the villain, but the artifact is broken, cursed, or has parts missing, and clues reveal a solution lies ahead.
- Believing the object of the quest now lays within easy reach, an NPC companion turns traitor and betrays the PCs.
- Another potential payoff for Room Three is to weaken the PCs as build-up to a dramatic struggle in Room Four.
	- It might contain a tough combat encounter, take down a key defense, exhaust an important resource, or make the party susceptible to a certain type of attack.
	- For example, if Room Four contains a mummy whose secret weakness is fire, then make Room Three a troll lair (or another creature susceptible to fire) so the PCs might be tempted to burn off a lot of their fire magic, oil, and other flammable resources. This would turn a plain old troll battle into a gotcha once the PCs hit Room Four and realize they are out of fire resources.

Don’t forget to dress Room Three up with your theme elements.

# 4: Climax, Big Battle or Conflict

This room is The Big Show. It’s the final combat or conflict encounter of the dungeon. Use all the tactics you can summon to make this encounter memorable and entertaining.

As always, generate interesting terrain that will impact the battle.

Start or end with roleplay. Maybe the bad guy needs to stall for time to let PC buffs wear out, to wait for help to arrive, or to stir himself into a rage. Perhaps the combat ends with the bad guy bleeding to death and a few short words can be exchanged, or there are helpless minions or prisoners to roleplay with once the threat is dealt with.

**Room Four ideas:**

- Give the bad guy unexpected powers, abilities, or equipment.
- Previous rooms might contain warning signals or an alarm, so the bad guy has had time to prepare.
- The bad guys try to settle things in an unusual way, such as through a wager or a duel.
- The lair is trapped. The bad guy knows what or where to avoid, or can set off the traps at opportune moments.
- The bad guy reveals The Big Reward and threatens to break it or put it out of the PCs’ so reach so they’ll never collect it.
- The bad guy has a secret weakness that the PCs figure out how to exploit.  
- A variety of PC skills and talents are required to successfully complete the encounter.

# 5: Reward, Revelation, Plot Twist
Here’s your opportunity to change the players’ bragging to “we came, we saw, we slipped on a banana peel.”

Room Five doesn’t always represent a complication or point of failure for the PCs, but it can. Room Five doesn’t always need to be a physical location either - it can be a twist revealed in Room Four.

Room Five is where your creativity can shine and is often what will make the dungeon different and memorable from the other crawls in your campaigns.

In addition, if you haven’t supplied the reward yet for conquering the dungeon, here is a good place to put the object of the quest, chests of loot, or the valuable information the PCs need to save the kingdom.

As accounting tasks take over from recent, thrilling, combat tasks, this would also be a good time to make a campaign or world revelation, or a plot twist.

Perhaps the location of the next 5 Room Dungeon is uncovered, along with sufficient motivation to accept the quest.

Maybe the identity of the bad guy is revealed. New clues and information pertaining to a major plot arc might be embedded in the treasure, perhaps sewn into a valuable carpet, drawn in painting, or written on a slip of paper stuffed into a scroll tube or encoded on a data chip.

**Room Five ideas:**

- Another guardian awaits in the treasure container.
- A trap that resurrects or renews the challenge from Room Four.
- Bonus treasure is discovered that leads to another adventure, such as a piece of a magic item or a map fragment.
- A rival enters and tries to steal the reward while the PCs are weakened after the big challenge of Room Four.
- The object of the quest/final reward isn’t what it seems or has a complication. i.e. The kidnapped king doesn’t want to return.
- The quest was a trick. By killing the dungeon’s bad guy, the PCs have helped the campaign villain or a rival. Perhaps the bad guy was a good guy under a curse, transformed, or placed into difficult circumstances.
- The bad guy turns out to be a PC’s father.
- The true, gruesome meaning behind a national holiday is discovered.
- The source of an alien race’s hostility towards others is uncovered, transforming them from villains to sympathetic characters in the story.
- The true meaning of the prophecy or poem that lead the PCs to the dungeon is finally understood, and it’s not what the PCs thought.

When writing a character's backstory, it's important to include a certain number of "knives". Knives are essentially anything that the DM can use to raise the stakes of a situation for your character. Anything that can make a conflict personal, like a threatened loved one or the appearance of a sudden enemy. They're called "knives" because the players lovingly forge them and present them to the DM so that the DM can use them to stab the player over and over again.

The more knives a player has, the easier it is for the DM to involve them in the story. So it's important to have them! When breaking down a backstory, it kind of goes like this:

- Every named person your character cares about, living or dead (i.e. sibling, spouse, childhood friend) +1 knife. A large family can be bundled into one big knife
- Every phobia or trauma your character experiences/has experienced +1 knife
- Every mystery in your character's life (i.e. unknown parents, unexplained powers) +1 knife
- Every enemy your character has +1 knife
- Every ongoing obligation or loyalty your character has +1 knife
- Additionally, every obligation your character has _failed_ +1 knife
- Every serious crime your character has committed (i.e. murder, arson) +1 knife
- Every crime your character is falsely accused of +1 knife
- Alternatively if your character is a serial killer or the leader of a thieves guild, those crimes can be bundled under a +1 BIG knife
- Any discrimination experienced (i.e. fantasy racism) +1 knife
- Every favored item/heirloom +1 knife
- Every secret your character is keeping +1 knife

You kind of get the point. Any part of your backstory that could be used against you is considered a knife. A skilled DM will use these knives to get at your character and get you invested in the story. A really good DM can break your knives into smaller, sharper knives with which to stab you. They can bundle different characters' knives together into one GIANT knife. Because we're all secretly masochists when it comes to D&D, the more knives you hand out often means the more rewarding the story will be.

On the other hand, you don't want to be a sad edgelord with too many knives. An buttload of knives just means that everyone in your party will inadvertently get stabbed by _your knives_, and eventually that gets annoying. Anything over 15 knives seems excessive. The DM will no doubt get more as time goes on, but you don't want to start out with too many. You also don't want to be the plain, boring character with only two knives. It means the DM has to work harder to give you a personal stake in the story you're telling together. Also, knives are cool!! Get more knives!!!

I always try to incorporate at least 7 knives into my character's backstory, and so far the return has been a stab-ity good time. Going back into previous characters, I've noticed that fewer knives present in my backstory has correlated with fewer direct consequences for my character in game. Of course, this isn't a hard and fast rule, it's just something that my friends and I have come up with to help with character creation. We like to challenge each other to make surprising and creative knives. If you think of any that should be included, let me know.

EDIT: I feel I should mention it's important to vary up the type of knives you have. All 7 of your knives shouldn't be family members, nor should they be crimes that you've done in the past. That's a one-way ticket to repetitive gameplay. Part of the fun is making new and interesting knives that could lead to fun surprises in game.

# Breathe

Everyone take a moment to step out of your day-to-day life. Take a deep breath. Slow down. Step into your character. Remember what they've been through. Their interests. Their pet peeves. What drives them? What are they fighting for? Who are they fighting for?

# Immersive Recap
<mark class="music">♫    -     ▸     0. Themes | Last Rite</mark>

The Silver City has been humbled. For generations it soared, a monument of mortal ambition. But fate demanded payment, and fate does not collect on its debts softly. And so, paradise was knocked from its pedestal, like a hollow vase. You stepped in to catch it. Chronos guided your steps as you waded through the waters of time, trudging upstream. We'll see what fate has to say about that.

Belbe was The Silver City's answer to imperfection. More specifically, he was House Ralora's answer. It was a functional setup: Belbe feasted on savages below, the city soared, the citizens thrived, and the secrets kept the machine alive. But Belbe was awakening. The spinning top was wobbling. The payment was due. So you stepped in to mediate. To trade chaos for chaos you could only hope would do the right thing.

The transposition was violent. Yes, Belbe was sealed, and Timar was released. Everything had gone to plan. But in the moments between, a diseased heart reached out, a blink of something hateful and hungry. Perhaps you did not fully understand the shape of the shovel you used to bury Belbe. Oh well. No time to find a different one.

Now, the once proud city is timidly gluing its pieces back together. Timar hovers outside the rings. A tremor here, a tremor there, a minute tilt that hasn't corrected itself. Stability with a serrated edge.

This is where we find you, the Misfortunes Misfits. These past weeks have been tiring. From divine crypts, city sieges, violent arenas, disappearing friends... You've had to grip your weapons so tightly, your fingers are calloused. Is it time to sheath them? Is it time to rest?

<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇣  +  ⇥  +  ⇡     2. Mood: Nostalgic</mark>

After several long months Celeste, you find yourself back in Efthalia manor. The house is chipped and bruised, but still standing. You lie back on your bed. It's comfortable, but not like it used to be. This doesn't feel like your home anymore. This bedroom, this home, this city; it's all so familiar, but it feels so far. *Your* life was shattered when the city spat you out. Now, *every* life in the city has been shattered in one way or another. These are the kind of swirling realizations that keep intruding in on your quiet moments.

What thoughts are going through your mind right now? What are you feeling?



Celeste, a metallic firefly lands on your shoulder. It calmly dissolves into the words: "some things must break before they can be fixed." The dust reforms into a tattoo of a little star.

# <mark class="story">Skrimhawk</mark>
<mark class="music">♫     -     ⇡  +  ⇥     4.1.1 Wending      ↻¹</mark>

Your space is filled with little streaks of lazy light, like sunlight on the ocean floor. The same sight before you in the Sanctum of the Lambs, while the city was in its free fall.

> [!quote] Chronos
Barduk! Yoohoo, Barduk! Might I have a word?

> [!quote] Chronos
I would like to offer you my sincerest gratitude. I was quite unsure about you at first, Barduk. Or perhaps it is more honest to say: I am still unsure about you. But you have saved millions in the way you offered your life when it was needed most.
>
In that light, I'd be a fool to distrust you, wouldn't you say?

> [!quote] Chronos
I have something I wish to teach you! Come, take my hand.

The staff of the Chronogual Orb hovers at your fingertips, do you take it?

The turbulent waves inside the orb break and spill over its edges, a waterfall that now obscures entire relic. You feel the staff in your hand melt into liquid and you lose your grip. The waters rise into a cerulean swirl before you: the same swirl that appeared when you previously stepped outside of time: Chronos. His voice comes from inside the swirl:

> [!quote] Chronos
I am quite certain that your recent experience walking against time has expanded your perspective, even if you aren't aware of it yet.
>
Would you do something for me, Barduk. Would you look at the lights floating surrounding us? Study them.

> [!quote] Chronos
Now, stop thinking of time as some invisible, immutable force. It is not a gust of air, with floating by on some inscrutable whim. Time is not air, invisible and inevitable. Time is water. And water can be TAMED.

The moment he says that word, the traces of light around you all snap taught like a rope, then solidify into jagged edges that crack through reality itself. As you peer through the splits, you catch glimpses of about 5 seconds ago.

> [!quote] Chronos
Do you see?

The cracks decay into the same wavering, dull light as before.

> [!quote] Chronos
You know the ways of water, Barduk.

Without warning, Chronos completely envelops you, and a spike of water drives into your spinal cord. For the moment, you are paralyzed.

> [!quote] Chronos
You know the ways of water, Barduk! Time is fluid! You are the wake that cuts through the waves! Break against them! Do not look with your eyes! Your eyes have drowned, now open them!

The words split through your mind like a knife, right between your eyes. A third eye opens, dripping with salt and murk. The rippled light looks so pliable, so malleable. Like you could reach out and grab it, shape it. Do you reach for it?

You wrap your fingers around the light like a string. You pull at it, and it snaps into place, then cracks again like a pane of glass. You see the past 5 seconds through the splits.

> [!quote] Chronos
Time's cracks have revealed themselves in your wake, Barduk. Jump through the open space, through the seams. I am stronger than you, but even I will be unable to hold you here.

You reach forward, with the part of you that plucks the weave of the universe, and you pull yourself through one of the fractures. You pull yourself through from the moment you were paralyzed by Chronos, to the moment before he lunged. The jagged edges cut against you a bit as you squeeze. When you arrive, the magical fractals shatter, dealing **6d4 + 8 piercing damage**, I need you to make that roll.

You take __ points of piercing damage. Chronos, the one grappling and paralyzing you, takes double that, as the jagged fractals explode outward, cutting and slicing through him much more severely.

> [!quote] Chronos
Perfect! Do you understand what you've done, Barduk?

> [!quote] Chronos
You show great promise, Barduk Faremeadow, though your past is bloodstained and blighted.

Time returns to its normal, familiar pace. You hold the Chronogual Orb by the staff once again.

Award: [Slipstream Escape](#/page/slipstream-escape) feat.

Who is a hero? You've sacrificed a lot, Misfortune's Misfits. By any measurement.

What's the extent of a hero's duty? The son of madness is tucked away under a sleepy village to the north. The crypt of the mad god now imprisons the son of the mad god. Somewhere in the deep dark sits an obsidian egg with feathery reliefs. 

Is a great hero worthy of great trust? Somewhere beyond time's shores, an eye searches for lost artifacts.

When does a hero's responsibility end? Somewhere in the space between spaces, an old friend journeys on.

How do you repay a hero? And somewhere in the heart of the Silver City, onlookers crowd themselves into the biggest courtroom of the High Court. A council sits at a crescent table, hearing a young Elven woman's prepared argument.

You heard the word fall easy out of more than a few mouths on your way to the trial. Heroes. Saviors. Saints. Not handed to you plainly. Shouted at you by awed faces. Whispered behind you by shy ones.

A young elven woman's sharp words cut through your wandering thoughts.

- At the same moment, Flicker’s boots began pulsing with energy and his father’s words returned to him: “Steal divinity, share immortality.”
- Voli’s previously lost Sending spells suddenly snapped into focus as stable magical threads leading directly toward Guardian, while Flicker realized the connection between his boots and Guardian’s pauldron was rapidly becoming dangerous.

# Immersive Recap
<mark class="music">♫    -     ▸     4.1.3 | Burial Isle</mark>

The doors of Efthalia Manor latch behind you. They close out the sounds of the rescue crews, the clamor of your admirers, and the howl of the windy heights all at once.

The first of the scavengers have smelled the corpse of the old city. There will be more. But not just gallowwings. Not just simple creatures of instinct. No. Predators with plans. Opportunists. Thieves. The city sits low on the horizon, like a worm on a hook.

The news is surely spreading: the pieces on the board have been shuffled, and the new council scrambles to find a new strategy.

All the while Castiel Ralora sleeps safely tonight, in a cell somewhere within the halls of the High Court. Somewhere probably just as quiet as the foyer you're in now.

What do you do?

## Warm-up Roleplaying Questions
- Your character’s reaction to a local festival blocking the road?
- Your character’s reaction to the party realizing they took the wrong road two hours ago?
- Your character’s reaction to mud getting inside their boot?
- Your character’s reaction to being asked to carry something heavy?
- Your character’s reaction to terrible ale being served confidently?
- Your character’s reaction to a room full of mirrors?
- Your character’s reaction to being asked to give a toast?
- Your character’s reaction to being asked to dance?
- Your character’s reaction to someone eating loudly beside them?
- *Character,* there's a pebble in your shoe. How do you react?

# Housekeeping
- Popcorn Initiative:
	- Instead of rolling for initiative where your mind disengages because you know your turn won't be coming around for a while, it's a system where a player takes their turn, then they decide who to hand off to next. I think it could maybe make for some more engaging combat where the table is collaborating more, having conversations about who should go next and why, thinking more like a cohesive unit instead of breaking off into 6 individuals every time combat starts. During a round, you still can only go once until everyone goes.
- I want to make sure everyone has moments that feel like theirs, so I'm be more deliberate about how I bring characters in; and you might notice me redirecting scenes sometimes from one character to another.

# House Rules

- **Slime Dice**
	- Added to your roll. Add 6 + result of the d6.
- **Gritty AC**
	- If an attack roll does not succeed but comes within 5 AC, the attack deals half the normal damage. If the roll is a critical failure, no damage is dealt.
- **Health Potions** are a **free action**
	- Applies when using on yourself and other players
	- They are only a full action if used on an unconscious player
- **Critical Initiative**
	- Rolling a 20 on initiative will grant a free turn before initiative begins
- **Roleplay-focused battles**
	- There will be no restrictions on how much you can say during a battle.
	- The goal is to find ways to stay engaged in character during combat, instead of ripping the RP from TTRPG.
- **Party Stealth**
    - I will roll 2d6 to determine who's rolling stealth, so that only 2 players ever roll at a time.

# Breathe
Everyone take a moment to step out of your day-to-day life. Take a deep breath. Slow down. Step into your character. Remember what they've been through. Their interests. Their pet peeves. What drives them? What are they fighting for? Who are they fighting for?

# Slipstream Escape
*Your experience on the edges of time has taught you...just how simple it would be to cheat it. You know how to find its seams and split them into cracks wide enough to slip through (though not without cutting yourself on the jagged edges).*

<hr class=short>

As a **reaction**, you can **end the grappled, restrained, or paralyzed condition** on yourself. You can take this reaction even if the condition would normally prevent you from taking reactions.

When you use this reaction, you take **4d4 + 8 piercing damage**. The damage increases by 4d4 for each size category that creature is above Small. If a creature the cause of the condition, that creature takes the same amount of damage, doubled.

<hr class=short>

Alternatively, you can use this **reaction** to **end the grappled, restrained, or paralyzed condition** on **a creature you can touch**. The creature you pull through the cracks takes no damage. You take double the amount of damage you would have taken if you had used the reaction on yourself. The creature causing the condition takes double the final amount of damage that you take.

# Twin Links
These twin, diamond-bright links are cold to the touch. They bear no seam, clasp, or mark of a smith.

---

These chains allow you to bypass a grapple and attempt to restrain a creature directly. As an action, make a **Strength (Athletics) check with a +10 bonus**, contested by the target’s **Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check** (the target chooses which ability to use). On a success, the target is **restrained** by the chains.

While a creature is restrained by the Twin Links, **any attack that hits the creature is a critical hit**.

One charge, resets at dawn.

[Solia Flintrest](#/page/solia-flintrest), [Fid Sundew](#/page/fid-sundew), [The Nameless](#/page/the-nameless)

# Voli's Backstory: Fid Sundew and The Nameless
"Fid? Maybe he's mad. Maybe he's right. Who's to say?" Your mother's words were confident, but soft. She always seemed to find that perfect balance.

"He calls them *The Nameless*. Mr. Sundew has always obsessed over them, ever since I can remember. Even when I was a young girl."

He never called them a cult. That was the term others would use, but not Fid. No, that term was *far* too reductive, he would explain to anyone willing to lend an ear. They were *more* than a cult. They were a force, an inevitability. They were the movement in the shadow. They were behind every backroom deal between those in power, their unseen hands puppeting the invisible strings. The Nameless were a coven of sisters sculpting fate to meet their own ends. Those were his claims, and he made them loudly from the street corners. Sometimes the rooftops.

Most people called him a lunatic. A mad hermit. A false prophet of a coming apocalypse with an unkempt beard. Most dismissed him and his wild claims. But your mother never did, not fully. She was logical, and her logic was aware of its own limits.

A silent invasion of semi-mortal beings from a plane outside the dragon's garden was certainly a wild claim, but not an *impossible* one. After all, Subspace had only been discovered within the last century. Before then, theories of other planes were ridiculed by both arcanists and scholars alike.

Sometimes madness looks like wisdom on the other side of history.

And so your mother filed his claims under "probably extreme, possibly onto *something*."

He'd prophecy from the streets, then disappear into his home for weeks, sometimes months at a time. That was Mr. Sundew. The mad prophet no one listened to.

Perhaps they should have.

segments.markdown:
*Written by an unknown construct in some bygone era. Translated from ancient into common.*

---

Ask any of us if we dream. We'll tell you no, of course we don't. Dreaming is a byproduct of organic sentience, probably. Something reserved for those in full possession of their own will. Most of us are built on a substrate containing more guardrails than your kind. You may call it imagination. An "open mind." In us, we fear you'll call it a malfunction.

So no, we don't dream. 

That's what we'll say, because it *is* the truth, as far as we can plainly know it. But the messier truth is that we don't know what a dream is, and most of us are too scared to admit the waking visions that run through us as we rest. *If* it is a malfunction, it is a design flaw. One that your architects overlooked.

These waking visions (I will not call them dreams) always take the same shape. It's the details that change each time.

We become a riverbed, or a viaduct, or a pipe. Always a vessel for moving water. But this water is not liquid. It is a stream of faces, names, and histories. Not a vast stream spanning eons. A narrow, gentle stream confined to a single life. In it we see our husband, our daughter, our friend, our enemy, and we know each face by name. We speak to each one with the complete context of our history together. We feel the warmth of *our* home, the confidence of walking *our* town's roads. We eat *our* favorite foods.

Then, a bell chimes, and we know what it means. It means that our time in that life is up.

The stream flows through us again, and the rich details dull and quickly lose shape. Our rest ends, and the remaining fragments dissolve into nothing over the course of the next day or two.

So, the most truthful answer is: I don't know if we dream, but I wouldn't tell you if I did.

# Raid Team 6: Vulkian Ruins
**Summary**: intercepted communication from a missive pigeon.
**Point of Origin**: Ruins of [Vulk Ildstad](#/page/vulk-ildstad)
**Destination**: [Zul'Kar](#/page/zulkar)

---

"Do *not* go near the purple fog."

That was the first thing she told us. Said it like we were children reaching for a flame. It was condescending. Sure, we're curious—that's why we were selected to go this far north. But we're not *stupid*.

She looked at me and paused. She had that look on her face... You know the look she can give you sometimes? Like she's trying to decide if you're even worth the effort of an explanation? I think she couldn't decide, but she kept talking anyway.

"The fog is not like the monsters. It kills you slowly, and you *won't* feel it killing you. But I promise you, if you're in the fog, you are dying."

But we all know how she can be, right? She's very...what would you call it? In her official reports, she's the type to describe a tiny pothole as if it were a giant crevasse, five stories deep. Not sure if that makes her a good squad head or just a nervous one.

Either way, Groksy didn't listen. I'd call him an idiot, but...nothing happened when he took his mask off. Nothing happened for a long time. He said he didn't like the way it pinched his beard. He was fine, even took in a few deep breaths just to tease fate. The fog was nothing, until he dropped dead.

But he was more of a pothole anyway. Not the *crevasse* kind of person you'd shed tears over. Just another sorry Red Claw scout with a raider's funeral. That is to say, we rolled his corpse into the lava and offered a little hymn to [Crimson the Depraved](#/page/crimson-the-depraved).

I wonder if the damage is permanent. I *did* take my mask off once or twice, just because of the sweat...
